trial.title: An Integrated Intervention Using a Pill Ingestible Sensor System

endpoints.description: Acceptability to the integrated intervention will be evaluated by quantitative measures interviews. The items in the quantitative measure will be rated on five-item Likert scales ranging from very strongly disagree to very strongly agree. Domains to be assessed will include overall satisfaction (would recommend to friend, would use outside of study setting, satisfied with system), utility, and specific items such as helpfulness and convenience. In addition, the investigators will ask participants to rate items specific to the ID-Cap system (comfort of wristband, comfort receiving text messages).

endpoints.measure: Frequency and timeliness of SBDOH intervention, level of challenges of SBDOH in HIV treatment
endpoints.description: The investigators will collect SBDOH measures, such as economic stability (e.g., food security), health (e.g., gap in health coverage), neighborhood and built environment (e.g. transportation needs), social and community context (e.g., violence, and criminal justice involvement), and substance and alcohol use, sexual behavior, and other health related behaviors. Challenges of SBDOH will be measured as (i) the count of SBDOH issues one is facing, and (ii) the degree of each issue (e.g., low/medium/high with housing challenge) with summary scores. Frequency and timeliness of SBDOH intervention are measured as number of sessions, and time to first, and subsequent sessions, if applicable, from baseline, and others. This information will also be collected when intervention if triggered by the monitoring system.

endpoints.measure: Adherence to ART--percent of prescribed medication taken
endpoints.description: Adherence to ART measured by ID(identification)-Cap system for up to 20 weeks, defined as percent of prescribed medication taken

endpoints.measure: Self-Reported Medication Adherence--percent of prescribed dose taken
endpoints.description: The investigators will use a widely used measure of percent of prescribed dose taken during the preceding seven days. This measure is easy to use and has been significantly associated with virological and immunological outcomes.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06480578 is a Phase 2 randomized open-label study of an ingestible sensor system (ID-Cap ISS) integrated with SBDOH intervention vs usual care in 110 PLWH with suboptimal adherence.

Evidence base: Liu et al. 2022 (PMC9782816) conducted a similar RCT (NCT02797262) using the same ID-Cap system with real-time text reminders vs usual care in 112 participants over 16 weeks. This provides direct evidence for comparable endpoints.

Primary-0 (Acceptability): Liu et al. reported >90% overall satisfaction with the IS system. Nimbalkar et al. 2026 (wrist-worn Reader pilot) reported mean SUS score 78.0 (±9.4), indicating good acceptability. Evidence role: direct_numeric for acceptability metrics.

Primary-1 (SBDOH frequency/timeliness): No direct published data on SBDOH intervention frequency endpoints. Liu study did not measure SBDOH components. Evidence role: mechanism_background only; prediction based on intervention design and expected care coordination response to missed doses.

Primary-2 (ART adherence - ID-Cap): Liu et al. showed IPAM score higher in IS group (0.018, 95% CI: -0.098–0.134, p=0.75) and VL decayed faster (-0.020, 95% CI: -0.042–0.002, p=0.08). Adherence pattern sustained post-intervention. Evidence role: direct_numeric for adherence improvement direction.

Primary-3 (Self-reported adherence): Liu et al. used self-report as secondary measure; correlation with electronic monitoring established in HIV literature. Self-report typically higher than MEMS but strongly correlated. Evidence role: indirect_direction.

Primary-4 (Dosing patterns): Liu et al. used group-based trajectory modeling to characterize adherence patterns. Consecutive missed doses are standard adherence metric. Evidence role: indirect_direction.

Secondary-0 (Viral load): Liu et al. showed faster VL decay in IS group vs UC (p=0.08 trend). PrEPSteps RCT (PMC12974493) showed 14% higher adherence with intervention. Evidence role: direct_numeric for VL trajectory.

Secondary-1/2 (Sexual partners/condomless sex): No direct evidence from Liu et al. or related trials. These are exploratory behavioral endpoints. Evidence role: mechanism_background only; high uncertainty.

Key uncertainties: (1) SBDOH-specific outcomes not previously tested with ID-Cap; (2) Wrist-worn vs patch-based Reader differences; (3) 28-week follow-up longer than prior studies; (4) COVID-19 may impact implementation.

Population match: Liu study enrolled similar PLWH with suboptimal adherence from safety-net clinics. Drug regimens overlap (TDF/FTC, TAF/FTC, etc.). Endpoint definitions align for adherence and acceptability.
Evidence gaps: No published results for NCT06480578 itself; SBDOH intervention timing/frequency outcomes are novel; sexual behavior endpoints are exploratory.
Safety: Liu et al. reported IS system well tolerated. ID-Cap is FDA-cleared. No serious safety signals expected.
Trial outcome prediction: Likely to demonstrate improved adherence and acceptability based on prior ID-Cap RCT evidence. SBDOH integration adds complexity but builds on established platform.
